mainTopic: Collecting debts from heirs, buyers and guarantors: oral loans, handwritten notes, the guarantor's 'and', and the strangling case
overview: רב פפא rules that an oral loan (מלוה על פה) can be collected from the borrower's heirs but not from people who bought his land, because an oral loan has no קלא. רבי יוחנן adds that a note in the borrower's own handwriting reaches only free property, even if בית דין confirmed it. רמי בר חמא challenges this from רבי אלעזר's case of an unsigned גט handed over before witnesses. The גמרא answers that there the husband obligated himself from the time of writing. Next, רב explains the משנה about a guarantor (ערב): a guarantor's line joined to the document with 'and' (ופלוני ערב) reaches sold property, while 'פלוני ערב' standing alone reaches only free property. After a challenge from רבא, the גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן agrees with רב. רבי יוחנן also rules that the הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל, even in בן ננס's strangling case. Finally שמואל says a guarantor in the strangling case is bound if a קנין was made, which implies an ordinary ערב needs no קנין. רב נחמן disagrees, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An oral loan can be collected from heirs but not from buyers
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that a מלוה על פה can be collected from the borrower's heirs, so that people will keep lending. It cannot be collected from people who bought the borrower's land, because an oral loan is not publicly known.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The law is that a loan made by word of mouth can be collected from the heirs, but not from the buyers. It can be collected from the heirs so that we do not lock the door in front of borrowers. It cannot be collected from the buyers because such a loan has no publicity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the final הלכה about collecting an oral loan after the borrower dies or sells his land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heirs must pay, because otherwise lenders would be afraid to lend and people who need loans would be stuck. Buyers do not lose their land, because an oral loan has no קלא (publicity). A buyer had no way to know the land was tied up by this debt.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan made by word of mouth, with no signed document
Heirs of the borrower
Buyers who purchased the borrower's land
Locking the door: discouraging people from lending
Publicity, public knowledge of the loan

steps.whatToRemember: Oral loan: heirs pay (so people keep lending); buyers are protected (no קלא).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule: a lender can take land that was already sold only when the loan was publicly known. The rest of the sugya builds on that idea.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The law is:

phrases.aramaic: מִלְוֶה עַל פֶּה – גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין,
phrases.english: An oral loan – he collects from the heirs,
but he does not collect from the buyers.
He collects from the heirs –

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תִּנְעוֹל דֶּלֶת בִּפְנֵי לֹוִין,
phrases.english: so that you do not lock the door in front of borrowers,
and he does not collect from the buyers –
because it has no publicity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final ruling closing the earlier discussion about oral loans
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלוה על פה is collected from heirs (so people keep lending) but not from buyers (no publicity).

steps.title: Does confirming the handwriting in court help with sold property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a note in the borrower's own handwriting can be collected only from property he still owns (נכסים בני חורין). רבה בר נתן asks רבי יוחנן what happens if the handwriting was confirmed in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he brought out against him a note in his own handwriting saying he owes him money, he collects from free (unsold) property, and so on. רבה בר נתן asked רבי יוחנן: If the handwriting was confirmed in court, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a line from the משנה and sets up a question about it. רבה בר נתן asks whether court confirmation changes the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A note in the borrower's handwriting with no witnesses has no קלא, so it cannot take land from buyers. The question is whether בית דין confirming the handwriting gives the note enough public standing to reach sold land (נכסים משועבדים).

keyTerms.meaning: A note in the borrower's own handwriting, without signed witnesses
Free property: land the borrower still owns and has not sold
Was confirmed or established
He asked him

phrases.english: If he brought out against him a note in his own handwriting
that he owes him –
he collects from free property, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." means the משנה continues: but not from land that was already sold.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבָּהּ בַּר נָתָן מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Natan asked Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: הוּחְזַק כְּתַב יָדוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין, מַאי?
phrases.english: If his handwriting was confirmed in court, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבָּהּ בַּר נָתָן מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה about handwritten notes
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether court confirmation of a handwritten note lets the lender collect from sold property

steps.title: Court confirmation does not help
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that even when the handwriting is confirmed in בית דין, the lender collects only from free property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even if the handwriting was confirmed in court, he collects only from free property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers רבה בר נתן's question with a clear no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Confirmation proves the note is real, but it does not make the loan public in a way buyers could have known about. So buyers stay protected, just as with an oral loan.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
He collects only

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּחְזַק כְּתַב יָדוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין –
phrases.english: Even though his handwriting was confirmed in court –

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה אֶלָּא מִנְּכָסִים בְּנֵי חוֹרִין.
phrases.english: he collects only from free property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּחְזַק כְּתַב יָדוֹ בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Court confirmation does not allow collection from sold property; only free property.

steps.title: Challenge begins: the three invalid גיטין
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא starts a challenge to רבי יוחנן by quoting a משנה about three invalid גיטין. If the woman remarries using one of them, the child is still כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא objected: Three גיטין are invalid, but if she remarried, the child is כשר. These are: he wrote it in his own handwriting but no witnesses signed; witnesses signed but it has no date; it has a date but only one witness. These are the three invalid גיטין, and if she remarried, the child is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא opens an objection by quoting a משנה. This step is setup; the real punch comes in the next line, from רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case is the important one: a גט in the husband's own handwriting with no witnesses signed on it. That is just like a handwritten loan note. The next step will show what רבי אלעזר says about such a document.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection from a source
Invalid bills of divorce
She married (another man)
The child is valid, not a ממזר
Date written in the document

steps.confusionAlert: "Invalid" here does not mean the divorce is worthless. These גיטין should not be used, but if she already remarried, the child is כשר.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama objected:
Three bills of divorce are invalid,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in גיטין 86a.

phrases.english: but if she married, the child is valid.
And these are they:

phrases.aramaic: כָּתַב בִּכְתַב יָדוֹ – וְאֵין עָלָיו עֵדִים;
phrases.english: He wrote it in his own handwriting, but there are no witnesses on it;

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים – וְאֵין בּוֹ זְמַן;
phrases.english: there are witnesses on it, but there is no date in it;

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ בּוֹ זְמַן – וְאֵין בּוֹ אֶלָּא עֵד אֶחָד;
phrases.english: there is a date in it, but it has only one witness;
these are three invalid bills of divorce,
and if she married, the child is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an objection against רבי יוחנן's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a confirmed handwritten note cannot reach sold property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a משנה about a handwritten גט without witnesses; the attack is completed by רבי אלעזר in the next step

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: an unsigned document handed over before witnesses collects from sold property
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that a גט with no signed witnesses, but handed over in front of witnesses, is valid, and she can collect from sold property. This is the heart of רמי בר חמא's challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Even though there are no witnesses on it, as long as he gave it to her in front of witnesses, it is valid, and she collects from sold property.
steps.whatsHappening: This completes רמי בר חמא's challenge. רבי אלעזר allows collection from sold land based on a document with no signed witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a document without signatures can take sold land just because witnesses saw it handed over, then a handwritten note confirmed in בית דין should surely be able to as well. That contradicts רבי יוחנן. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He handed it to her in front of witnesses
Property that was tied to the debt and later sold to buyers
Valid

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: confirmed handwriting reaches only free property. Challenge: רבי אלעזר lets a witness-less document reach sold property if it was handed over before witnesses.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו עֵדִים,
phrases.english: Even though there are no witnesses on it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ לָהּ בִּפְנֵי עֵדִים – כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: but he gave it to her in front of witnesses – it is valid,
and she collects from sold, obligated property.
phrases.notes: She is collecting what her כתובה owes her, even from land the husband already sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection set up in step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A document with no signed witnesses, handed over before witnesses, collects from sold property. So a handwritten note confirmed in בית דין should surely collect from sold property too.

steps.title: The גט case is different because the husband committed from the time of writing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רמי בר חמא. In the גט case the husband tied up his property from the moment it was written, so that case says nothing about a handwritten note confirmed later in בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different, because from the time of writing he obligated himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רמי בר חמא's challenge and defends רבי יוחנן. The גט case and the handwritten-note case are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband wrote the גט, he already planned to hand it over in front of witnesses, so his property was tied up (משועבד) for her כתובה from the very start. The borrower who wrote a note in his own hand never planned on confirming it in בית דין. Confirming it later cannot reach back in time and create a lien on property he already sold.

keyTerms.meaning: There it is different: the case you brought does not compare to ours
The time the document was written
He obligated himself, tying up his property to the debt

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets an important rule: a lien on sold property depends on what the obligor intended when the document was made, not on what was done with the document later.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: "There" means רבי אלעזר's case of the גט handed over in front of witnesses, from Step 5.

phrases.english: for from the time of writing
he obligated himself.
phrases.notes: "He" is the husband. He knew from the start that the גט would be handed over in front of witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר חמא's challenge from Steps 4–5 and defends רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses at the handing over of a גט allow collection from sold property, so confirming handwriting in בית דין should do the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the גט case the husband intended the obligation from the time of writing. A handwritten note confirmed later was never meant that way, so it reaches only free property.

steps.title: רב rules on a guarantor written before or after the signatures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a guarantor whose commitment appears after the witnesses signed. רב then explains: if it is written before the signatures, the lender collects even from sold property. If it is written after, he collects only from free property.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a guarantor who appears after the signing of documents, etc. רב said: before the signing of documents, he collects from sold (liened) property. After the signing of documents, he collects only from free property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה, about a guarantor (ערב). רב explains the rule for a guarantor written before and after the witnesses' signatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the guarantor's line is written above the witnesses' signatures, the witnesses cover it. That makes it public, like a regular signed note, so the lender can take sold property. If it is written below the signatures, no witness covers it. It works like an oral obligation and reaches only property the guarantor still owns.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarantor: someone who promises to pay if the borrower does not
The signing of the document by the witnesses
Liened property that has already been sold to others
Free property the person still owns

steps.confusionAlert: "Before" and "after" the signing refers to where the guarantor's line sits in the document: above the witnesses' signatures or below them.

phrases.english: A guarantor who appears
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה.

phrases.english: after the signing of the documents, etc.
Rav said:
Before the signing of the documents,
he collects from liened property.
After the signing of the documents,
he collects from free property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה, about guarantors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guarantor written before the witnesses' signatures is collectible from sold property. One written after is collectible only from free property.

steps.title: A second version of רב: even before the signatures, only free property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that at other times רב said that even a guarantor written before the signatures is collectible only from free property.
steps.simpleTranslation: At other times רב said: even before the signing of documents, he collects only from free property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling of רב that seems to clash with the first. This sets up the contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, רב let the lender take sold property when the guarantor was written before the signatures. Here רב says that even in that case he takes only free property. The two rulings disagree about the very same case.

keyTerms.meaning: At other times
He collects only from

phrases.english: At other times Rav said:
Even before the signing of the documents,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה אֶלָּא מִנְּכָסִים בְּנֵי חוֹרִין.
phrases.english: he collects only from free property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second ruling of רב that conflicts with his ruling in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a guarantor written before the signatures is collectible only from free property.

steps.title: רב contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רב's two rulings contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: רב contradicts רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the problem outright: רב's two rulings about a guarantor written before the signatures cannot both be right as they stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ruling allows collecting from sold property, and the other allows only free property, for the same case. The גמרא needs a way to show the two rulings are about different situations.

keyTerms.meaning: A contradiction between one statement of רב and another statement of רב

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: Rav against Rav!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the ruling of Step 8 against the ruling of Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's two rulings about a guarantor written before the signatures
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same case, a guarantor written before the signatures, gets two opposite results from the same אמורא.

steps.title: The difference is the word "and"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the contradiction. "פלוני ערב" stands on its own, so it reaches only free property. "ופלוני ערב" joins the main document, so it reaches sold property.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling is where it was written "So-and-so is a guarantor." That ruling is where it was written "And so-and-so is a guarantor."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב's two rulings are about two different wordings of the guarantor's line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the document says "פלוני ערב" with no "and," it reads like a separate statement, and the witnesses' signatures do not clearly cover it, so only free property can be taken. If it says "ופלוני ערב," the "and" ties it to the loan document. The signatures then cover it, and sold property can be taken.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: the two sources can both be right
So-and-so: a stand-in for any name
The connecting letter ו ("and"), which ties a phrase to what came before

steps.whatToRemember: A guarantor's line written before the signatures reaches sold property only if it is joined to the document ("ופלוני ערב"). Written as a separate line ("פלוני ערב"), or after the signatures, it reaches only free property.
steps.whyThisMatters: One letter, the ו, decides whether the witnesses' signatures cover the guarantor. That in turn decides whether buyers of his land can lose it.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this is where it was written in it "So-and-so is a guarantor."
phrases.notes: This matches the ruling in Step 8: free property only.

phrases.english: that is where it was written in it "And so-and-so is a guarantor."
phrases.notes: The extra "and" hooks this line onto the loan document, so the witnesses' signatures cover it too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (הא בהא), based on the document's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's two rulings are about the same case and clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: "ופלוני ערב" is part of the signed document and reaches sold property. "פלוני ערב" is separate and reaches only free property.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a guarantor is collected only from free property
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that whether the guarantor clause comes before or after the witnesses' signatures, the lender collects only from free property. The גמרא adds that this holds even when the document says 'ופלוני ערב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: In both this case and that case, the lender collects only from free property. And this is so even if the document says 'and so-and-so is a guarantor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion, from רבי יוחנן, about collecting from a guarantor. He is stricter on the lender than רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that 'ופלוני ערב' joins the main document, so the lender can collect even from sold property. רבי יוחנן disagrees: the guarantor clause never reaches sold property, whether it is written before or after the signatures. The גמרא's added comment says this applies even with the joining word 'ו'.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that, meaning before the signatures and after them
Free property: property the guarantor still owns and has not sold
And even though

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Both this and that,
phrases.notes: He means a guarantor written before the witnesses' signatures and one written after them.

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה אֶלָּא מִנְּכָסִים בְּנֵי חוֹרִין,
phrases.english: he collects only from free property,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דִּכְתִב בֵּיהּ ״וּפְלוֹנִי עָרֵב״.
phrases.english: and even though it is written in it 'and so-and-so is a guarantor.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רב's conclusion in Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, a guarantor clause allows collection only from free property, wherever it appears and even with 'ופלוני ערב'.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוחנן's own ruling about a greeting in a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא: witnesses signed under a greeting written in a גט make the גט invalid. רבי אבהו reports that רבי יוחנן explained 'שאילו' is invalid but 'ושאילו' is valid. So the 'and' does connect a clause to the main document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: If witnesses are signed under a greeting in a גט, the גט is invalid, because we worry that they signed only on the greeting. And רבי אבהו said: רבי יוחנן himself explained this to me. If it says 'Send greetings,' it is invalid. If it says 'And send greetings,' it is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רבי יוחנן using a ruling that רבי יוחנן himself explained about a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the גט case, רבי יוחנן holds that adding 'and' to the greeting ties it to the main text, so the signatures cover the whole גט. If so, 'ופלוני ערב' should also tie the guarantor to the main loan document. Then the lender should be able to collect from sold property, which contradicts Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source
A greeting line
We are concerned
It was explained to me personally
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about גיטין for its own sake. He is using רבי יוחנן's 'and' rule from the גט to show that 'ופלוני ערב' should also count as part of the loan document.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
Witnesses who are signed on a greeting
in a bill of divorce, it is invalid;

phrases.aramaic: חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא עַל שְׁאֵילַת שָׁלוֹם חָתְמוּ.
phrases.english: we are concerned that perhaps they signed only on the greeting.
And Rabbi Abahu said,

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: it was explained to me by Rabbi Yochanan himself:
'Send greetings': it is invalid.
'And send greetings': it is valid!
phrases.notes: The extra 'and' links the greeting to the גט, so the witnesses are seen as signing on everything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the added comment in Step 11 that the rule applies even with 'ופלוני ערב'
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן limits the lender to free property even when the document says 'ופלוני ערב'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן himself holds that 'and' ties a clause to the main document, as with 'ושאילו' in a גט. So 'ופלוני ערב' should tie the guarantor to the loan and reach sold property.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was speaking only about 'פלוני ערב' without the 'and'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that here too, רבי יוחנן's ruling covers only a document that says 'פלוני ערב', without 'and'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is a case where it was written 'so-and-so is a guarantor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves רבא's challenge. It narrows רבי יוחנן's ruling to the case without the word 'and'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comment in Step 11, 'even with ופלוני ערב', is dropped. רבי יוחנן's rule now matches his גט ruling. Without 'and', the guarantor clause stands alone and reaches only free property. With 'and', it joins the loan document and reaches sold property.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too
So-and-so is a guarantor (without the 'and')

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רבי יוחנן agrees with the 'and' principle. 'פלוני ערב' reaches only free property. 'ופלוני ערב' is part of the document and can reach sold property.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer takes back the earlier comment in Step 11. רבי יוחנן's ruling does NOT apply when the document says 'ופלוני ערב'.

phrases.english: Here too, it is where it was written 'so-and-so is a guarantor.'
phrases.notes: Notice there is no 'and' here, so the guarantor line stands alone, just like 'שאילו' in the גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in Step 12 by limiting רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) and dropping the added comment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן limits collection to free property even with 'ופלוני ערב'
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן's ruling applies only to 'פלוני ערב'. With 'ופלוני ערב', the lender collects even from sold property, just as with 'ושאילו' in a גט.

steps.title: Now רבי יוחנן just repeats רב
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן only meant 'פלוני ערב' without 'and', his ruling is the same as רב's. So why was he presented as disagreeing?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is the same as רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the answer it just gave in Step 13. If רבי יוחנן is only talking about 'פלוני ערב', he is saying exactly what רב said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10, רב said 'פלוני ערב' reaches only free property. Step 13 limited רבי יוחנן to that same case. So the two now agree, yet רבי יוחנן's statement was presented as a separate, opposing view.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
That is the same as

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רבי יוחנן is only talking about 'פלוני ערב', without 'and', as Step 13 said.

phrases.english: this is the same as רב's view!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the result of Step 13's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The way רבי יוחנן's statement was presented as a separate view (Step 11)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After Step 13, רבי יוחנן's ruling matches רב's exactly, so it should not be presented as a different opinion.

steps.title: Read it as 'and so said רבי יוחנן'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the introduction: רבי יוחנן is agreeing with רב, not arguing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: And so said רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by fixing how רבי יוחנן's statement is introduced. He is not disagreeing with רב; he is agreeing with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing changes in the actual law. Only the framing changes, from 'רבי יוחנן said' as an opposing view to 'and so said רבי יוחנן', which marks support. רבי יוחנן's ruling now backs up רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead; read it this way
And so said; introduces someone who agrees

steps.whatToRemember: רב and רבי יוחנן agree: 'פלוני ערב' (no 'and') reaches only free property, while 'ופלוני ערב' joins the document and reaches sold property.

phrases.english: Say instead: And so said רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14's objection
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the introduction of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was arguing with רב

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל despite his praise
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה's story: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי ישמעאל, even though רבי ישמעאל praised בן ננס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'An incident came before רבי ישמעאל, etc.' רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Even though רבי ישמעאל praised בן ננס, the הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves back to the משנה's story and quotes its opening words. Then it brings רבי יוחנן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל's original view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי ישמעאל said a guarantor written after the signatures pays from free property. בן ננס said he does not pay at all, and רבי ישמעאל praised him. You might think the praise means רבי ישמעאל gave in. רבי יוחנן says no: the הלכה is like רבי ישמעאל's first ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident; a story of an actual case
Praised
The final law follows his view
The תנא who argued with רבי ישמעאל in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל's praise of בן ננס does NOT mean the הלכה follows בן ננס. The הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה וּבָא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: The משנה said: 'An incident came before רבי ישמעאל, etc.'
רבה בר בר חנה said
that רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקִּילֵּס רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אֶת בֶּן נַנָּס,
phrases.english: Even though רבי ישמעאל praised בן ננס,
the הלכה follows him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' means רבי ישמעאל: the guarantor pays from free property, but not from sold property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקִּילֵּס רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אֶת בֶּן נַנָּס, הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next part of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל: a guarantor written after the signatures pays from free property only.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law for a guarantor written after the signatures.

steps.title: Did רבי ישמעאל argue about the strangling case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי ישמעאל would say about בן ננס's case of someone strangling a debtor.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: In the strangling case, what would רבי ישמעאל say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about בן ננס's other example from the משנה, the strangling case (חנוק). It wants to know if רבי ישמעאל disagreed there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן ננס gave a case where someone was choking a debtor in the street, and a passerby said, 'Leave him, I'll pay.' בן ננס said the passerby is exempt. The question is whether רבי ישמעאל might agree in that case, even though he disagreed about a normal guarantor written after the signatures.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the Sages
The strangling case: someone choking a debtor in the street to make him pay

phrases.english: A question was asked:

phrases.aramaic: בְּחָנוּק – מָה לִי אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל?
phrases.english: In the strangling case, what would רבי ישמעאל say?
phrases.notes: This is בן ננס's example of a passerby who promises to pay so the creditor stops choking the debtor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בְּחָנוּק מָה לִי אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רבי ישמעאל's view reaches, now that the הלכה follows him
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי ישמעאל disagreed with בן ננס in the strangling case too, or agreed there

steps.title: Yes, he argued even there
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that רבי ישמעאל disagreed even in the strangling case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי ישמעאל disagreed even in the strangling case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a report from רבי יוחנן. רבי ישמעאל argued with בן ננס even about the strangling case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So רבי ישמעאל did not agree with בן ננס in any case. Even the passerby who promises to pay is obligated in his view. This answers what רבי ישמעאל held, but not yet whether the הלכה follows him there.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a source that answers the question
He disagreed

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for רבי יעקב said that רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: חָלוּק הָיָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אַף בְּחָנוּק.
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל disagreed even in the strangling case.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ישמעאל disagreed with בן ננס even in the strangling case.

steps.title: Is the הלכה like him in the strangling case?
steps.stepSummary: Now that we know רבי ישמעאל argued there, does the הלכה follow him in that case too?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the הלכה like him, or is the הלכה not like him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. Knowing what רבי ישמעאל held is one thing; it now asks whether the law actually follows him in the strangling case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said the הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל in general. But the strangling case might be different. Maybe there the הלכה follows בן ננס, even though רבי ישמעאל disagreed.

keyTerms.meaning: The law does not follow him

phrases.english: Is the הלכה like him,
phrases.notes: This means: like רבי ישמעאל, in the strangling case.

phrases.english: or is the הלכה not like him?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ, אוֹ אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question built on Step 18's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the practical law follows רבי ישמעאל in the strangling case

steps.title: The הלכה follows him even in the strangling case
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי ישמעאל disagreed even in the strangling case, and the הלכה follows him there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי ישמעאל disagreed even in the strangling case, and the הלכה follows him even in the strangling case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רבין's report from רבי יוחנן. The הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל even in the strangling case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין's report repeats what רבי יעקב said, that רבי ישמעאל disagreed. Then it adds the new piece: the הלכה is like him there too. So the passerby who says 'Leave him, I'll pay' is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל in every case, even the strangling case. A guarantor who commits after the loan, even a passerby who promises to pay, is obligated, and pays from free property.

phrases.english: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for when רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: חָלוּק הָיָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אַף בְּחָנוּק,
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל disagreed even in the strangling case,
and the הלכה follows him even in the strangling case.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּכִי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה follows רבי ישמעאל even in the strangling case.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי ישמעאל's ruling has no exceptions in practice, even in בן ננס's strongest example.

steps.title: שמואל: In the strangling case, a guarantor with a קנין is obligated
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל. If the debtor was being 'strangled' and a קנין was done with the person who promised to pay, that person is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If the debtor was being grabbed by the throat, and they made a קנין with the guarantor, he is obligated to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל about the 'strangling' case from the משנה. It is the case where someone grabs a debtor in the street and another person says 'leave him, I'll pay.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the strangling case, the guarantor's promise comes after the loan was already given. The lender gave nothing because of his promise. שמואל says such a promise does work, but only if a קנין was done with the guarantor.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Strangled.' The case where a lender grabs the debtor by the throat in the street, and someone else steps in and promises to pay.
They made a קנין with him. This is a formal act of acquisition that makes a commitment binding.
He becomes obligated (legally bound) to pay.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If the debtor was being strangled, and they made an act of acquisition with him (the guarantor),
he becomes obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יוחנן's rulings to a new אמורא's ruling on the same strangling case. Here a קנין was done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the strangling case, a guarantor who made a קנין is obligated to pay.

steps.title: So an ordinary guarantor does not need a קנין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a lesson from שמואל's words. Only the strangling case needs a קנין, so an ordinary ערב does not need one.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn from this that a regular guarantor does not need a קנין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads between the lines of שמואל's ruling and draws a lesson about a regular ערב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל needed a קנין only because this was the strangling case, where the promise came after the loan. So a regular ערב, who promises at the time the money is lent, is obligated even without a קנין. The lender gave the money because he trusted that promise.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From the general implication.' This tells you an inference is being drawn from what was said.
A guarantor. Someone who promises to pay if the borrower doesn't.
'In general.' Here it means an ordinary, regular case.
A formal act of acquisition that makes a deal or obligation binding.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think שמואל requires a קנין for every guarantor. The קנין is needed only in the strangling case. The whole point of this inference is that a regular ערב does not need one.

phrases.english: By inference, an ordinary guarantor
phrases.notes: An 'ordinary' guarantor is one who promises at the time of the loan, unlike the strangling case.

phrases.english: does not require an act of acquisition.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלַל דְּעָרֵב בְּעָלְמָא לָא בָּעֵי קִנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implied rule out of שמואל's ruling in step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to שמואל, an ordinary ערב at the time of the loan is obligated without a קנין.

steps.title: This argues with רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this lesson from שמואל disagrees with רב נחמן. It then begins to quote רב נחמן's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רב נחמן, because רב נחמן said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us that רב נחמן disagrees and is about to quote his statement, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point here is that the lesson from step 22 is not agreed by everyone. רב נחמן holds differently about whether a guarantor needs a קנין. We will see his exact words in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it disagrees.' The גמרא uses this to show that one view argues with another.
An אמורא whose opinion on guarantors is about to be quoted.
'For he said.' This introduces the quote that proves the disagreement.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Nachman,
as Rav Nachman said:

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the lesson from step 22 against רב נחמן's view, which is about to be quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inference from שמואל (no קנין for an ordinary ערב) is disputed by רב נחמן.
